entries.proposition: The review pools 43 studies and 197 patients, nearly all case reports and series, and says it included them because treatment publications are scarce.
entries.snippet: We decided to include case reports and case series because of the scarcity of publications on treatments for KCNT1‐related epilepsy

entries.proposition: No response threshold was used: a treatment counted as beneficial if frequency, duration or intensity fell, or quality of life improved, or if it was reported as beneficial even without details, or temporarily effective.
entries.snippet: we did not utilize a threshold (e.g., 50% reduction) to determine benefit as this information was not available in most published articles

entries.proposition: Evidence levels: two studies of quinidine at the top level, one at level 2, one each at level 3 for cannabidiol and quinidine, all the rest level 4.
entries.snippet: the remaining studies had a level of proof of 4

entries.proposition: Quinidine benefit was reported in 25 of 56 infants with migrating focal seizures (44.6 percent), and in none of 8 patients with sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy.
entries.snippet: None of the 8 patients observed any benefit from treatment with QUIN.

entries.proposition: The authors state persistence of benefit at 3 months was almost never documented and, where documented, was very low.
entries.snippet: the persistence of benefit at 3 months was almost never documented, and when it was, the persistence of efficacy at 3 months was very low

entries.proposition: The authors note that the natural history is not considered in most reports: seizures tend to decrease over time, so a drug started shortly before that decline may be credited with it.
entries.snippet: There is a tendency for most patients with KCNT1‐related epilepsy to have a reduction in seizures over time, and if a therapy is initiated shortly before this natural decrease, both patients and families may attribute a reduction in seizures to a medication, when the effect is actually due to the normal course of the disease.

entries.proposition: The authors name expectation as a bias: parents who have waited long for a treatment may report benefit.
entries.snippet: This can lead to biases, such as the placebo effect which can be significant for parents who have been waiting so long for a treatment with high expectations on the benefit for their child.

entries.proposition: Subgroup fishing: benefit did not differ between variants in functional domains and others (19 of 44 against 6 of 12, p 0.75), but a regrouping of two domains gave 12 of 16 against 13 of 40 (p 0.007).
entries.snippet: Interestingly, we observed a statistical difference when RCK2 + NAD were grouped together versus the rest of the mutations (Fisher's exact test performed, 12/16 vs. 13/40, p = 0.007), as suggested by Fitzgerald et al.

entries.proposition: In vitro and in vivo responses to quinidine disagreed for several of 14 variants tested in cells.
entries.snippet: Fourteen mutations have been examined in vitro, with in vitro and in vivo discrepancies in the response.

entries.proposition: Cardiac conduction harm (QT prolongation in 7 of 31 non-responders) and the need for intensive monitoring are stated limits on use.
entries.snippet: the risk of potentially fatal cardiac arrythmias secondary to QUIN use, as well as the need for intensive monitoring, may limit the utility of this drug in practice

entries.proposition: Cannabidiol and ketogenic diet were always prescribed together in the migrating-focal-seizure group, so their separate effects cannot be told apart.
entries.snippet: CBD was always simultaneously prescribed with KD in EIMFS patients, making it difficult to discern the distinct benefit of either

entries.proposition: Conventional antiseizure medications were reported beneficial in about 10 percent of infants with migrating focal seizures, and combination effects could not be separated.
entries.snippet: it was impossible to determine the intrinsic value of each ASM

entries.proposition: The authors advise N-of-1 methodology and natural-history data for future evaluation of therapies.
entries.snippet: The use of N of 1 methodologies and a better knowledge of natural history will help to better evaluate future therapies.
